card.name: Turning point after 'not studied' statements
card.fires_on: The word right after a clause saying something was not studied or established, such as 'but', a comma, 'it' or 'been', where the text turns to a hedged counterpoint like 'may be appropriate'.

modes.label: But after not-studied clause
modes.description: The word 'but' or a comma follows a statement that data or studies are lacking, leading into a qualified positive point.
modes.example: Dosages higher than 24 mg/6 mg daily have not been investigated in randomized clinical trials<< but>> may be appropriate for some patients.

modes.label: Hedge after Although clause
modes.description: After an 'Although ... not ...' opening, the pole fires on the comma or the first words of the main clause.
modes.example: Although it has not been systematically established that doses above 6 mg have additional benefit<<,>> there was a general trend for greater effects

card.writes: It suppresses 'recommend' and 'suggestion' words, so the text that follows is less likely to be a recommendation.
card.plain: It marks the hinge in a sentence that says something was not studied and then adds a cautious 'but'.
